title: Entropy and Randomness
subtitle: Why randomness matters and how to generate it securely

content.text: Cryptographic security depends on unpredictable random numbers. Weak randomness has caused catastrophic breaks in real systems.

content.definition: Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generator. Suitable for key generation, nonces, and tokens.

content.code:
import os
import secrets

# Generate 32 cryptographically random bytes
key = os.urandom(32)
print(key.hex())

# Secure token for password reset links
token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
print(token)  # e.g., "jLDQvb3rFMBk9N2..."

# NEVER use random.random() for security
# import random
# random.random()  <- NOT CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY SECURE

content.text: Always use os.urandom() or the secrets module for security-critical randomness in Python. Never use the random module.

questions.question: Which Python function generates cryptographically secure random bytes?
questions.explanation: os.urandom() reads from the OS CSPRNG (/dev/urandom on Linux). The random module is not cryptographically secure.

faq.a: A Number used ONCE. A nonce is a random value that must never be reused with the same key. Reusing a nonce with stream ciphers or GCM can be catastrophic.

examples: Generating a secure password reset token with secrets.token_urlsafe()
